question: A team builds an ML pipeline that ingests real-time sensor data via Pub/Sub, processes it, trains an anomaly detector, and stores results for analytics. Which combination of services is most appropriate?
options: A. Pub/Sub → Dataflow (streaming) → Vertex AI (training & prediction) → BigQuery (analytics)
B. Pub/Sub → Dataproc → AutoML → Cloud Bigtable
C. Pub/Sub → BigQuery → AutoML → Cloud Functions
D. Pub/Sub → Cloud Storage → Vertex AI → Cloud Storage
correct: A. Pub/Sub → Dataflow (streaming) → Vertex AI (training & prediction) → BigQuery (analytics)
explanation: Dataflow is the canonical streaming processor on Google Cloud; Vertex AI is the unified ML platform for training and serving; BigQuery is the standard analytics store.

question: You want to use a no-code/low-code ML approach for tabular data with automated feature engineering and hyperparameter tuning. Which Vertex AI capability fits?
options: A. Vertex AI AutoML for tabular data
B. Vertex AI custom training with PyTorch only
correct: A. Vertex AI AutoML for tabular data
explanation: AutoML tabular automates preprocessing, model search, and tuning. Custom training is for users with their own training code; the other choices are not ML modeling services.

question: You want to run SQL-based ML training on data already in BigQuery without exporting it. Which feature should you use?
correct: A. BigQuery ML (CREATE MODEL ... ML.PREDICT())
explanation: BigQuery ML lets analysts train and run predictions on regression, classification, time-series, and even imported TensorFlow models using SQL.

question: To preprocess unstructured image files at scale into TFRecord shards before training, which managed service is most appropriate?
options: A. Dataflow (Apache Beam) running a batch pipeline
correct: A. Dataflow (Apache Beam) running a batch pipeline
explanation: Dataflow scales to large datasets and writes sharded TFRecord outputs to Cloud Storage in a portable, repeatable way.

question: Which Vertex AI capability lets you store and serve precomputed feature values to both training and online prediction with a single API?
correct: A. Vertex AI Feature Store
explanation: Vertex AI Feature Store provides offline (for training) and online (low-latency) feature serving, helping ensure training/serving parity.

question: What is the recommended Google Cloud service for orchestrating an end-to-end ML workflow as a DAG of components (data prep, training, evaluation, deployment)?
options: A. Vertex AI Pipelines (Kubeflow Pipelines on Vertex)
correct: A. Vertex AI Pipelines (Kubeflow Pipelines on Vertex)
explanation: Vertex AI Pipelines is the managed Kubeflow Pipelines runner for orchestrating reproducible ML workflows with caching and lineage.

question: To label thousands of images consistently before training, which service can route tasks to human labelers with quality controls?
options: A. Vertex AI Data Labeling Service
correct: A. Vertex AI Data Labeling Service
explanation: Vertex AI Data Labeling Service provides managed human-in-the-loop labeling with quality controls for images, text, and video datasets.

question: To compare two trained models on the same validation set and pick the better one before promoting to production, which Vertex AI feature is most useful?
options: A. Vertex AI Model Evaluation (with metric and confusion-matrix visualizations)
correct: A. Vertex AI Model Evaluation (with metric and confusion-matrix visualizations)
explanation: Vertex AI Model Evaluation produces standardized metrics and visualizations for tabular, image, text, and video models.

question: For very large batch predictions on TBs of data, which Vertex AI feature is preferred over real-time online prediction endpoints?
options: B. Vertex AI Online Prediction with maximum replicas
correct: A. Vertex AI Batch Prediction
explanation: Batch Prediction scales worker pools to score large datasets cost-effectively without paying for an always-on endpoint.

question: Which technique reduces overfitting by injecting random transformations of training images during training?
options: D. Reducing the training set size
correct: A. Data augmentation
explanation: Augmentation (flips, crops, color jitter, mixup, etc.) increases effective dataset diversity and improves generalization.

question: Your training fails because the dataset doesn't fit in a single GPU's memory. Which distributed-training strategy is most appropriate to scale across multiple GPUs on the same machine?
options: A. Mirrored strategy / DDP (data parallelism across GPUs)
correct: A. Mirrored strategy / DDP (data parallelism across GPUs)
explanation: Data parallel strategies (TF Mirrored, PyTorch DDP) replicate the model across GPUs and split the batch — the standard way to scale within a machine.

question: To improve a transformer language model's accuracy on customer-specific text without changing the base model's weights drastically, which approach is recommended?
options: A. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA / adapters) on the customer dataset
B. Train a new model from scratch on the small dataset
D. Use only zero-shot prompts and ignore the data
correct: A. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA / adapters) on the customer dataset
explanation: PEFT methods like LoRA fine-tune small added matrices instead of full weights, lowering compute cost and reducing overfitting on small custom datasets.

question: A model performs much worse on production data than on the validation set after a few months. What is the most likely cause and the first step to investigate?
options: A. Data drift / concept drift — set up Vertex AI Model Monitoring to detect feature skew and drift
B. The model file is corrupted
C. The model's hyperparameters changed automatically
correct: A. Data drift / concept drift — set up Vertex AI Model Monitoring to detect feature skew and drift
explanation: Vertex AI Model Monitoring detects training/serving skew (initial) and drift over time, alerting before silent quality regressions.

question: Which fairness metric considers whether a model's true-positive rate is similar across protected groups?
options: A. Equality of opportunity (a.k.a. equal true-positive rate)
correct: A. Equality of opportunity (a.k.a. equal true-positive rate)
explanation: Equality of opportunity requires equal TPR across protected groups, one of several common fairness definitions to evaluate alongside performance metrics.

question: For a regression task forecasting daily product demand, which evaluation metric is most appropriate when large errors should be penalized more than small ones?
correct: A. Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
explanation: RMSE penalizes large errors more than MAE because errors are squared before averaging. Accuracy/F1 are classification metrics.

question: To avoid leaking future information into training when working with time-series data, which split strategy must be used?
correct: A. Chronological (time-based) train/validation/test split
explanation: Time-based splits preserve causality: train on past data and validate/test on later data. Random shuffles leak future information.

question: Which AI/ML service on Google Cloud is best for managing fine-tuning, embeddings, and grounded generation with the latest foundation models (e.g., Gemini)?
options: A. Vertex AI Model Garden (and Vertex AI Studio for the generative models)
correct: A. Vertex AI Model Garden (and Vertex AI Studio for the generative models)
explanation: Vertex AI Model Garden hosts foundation and open-source models; Vertex AI Studio provides prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and grounding tooling for generative models.

question: To find sensitive PII inside text used for training (and redact or block it), which Google Cloud service helps?
options: A. Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP)
correct: A. Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP)
explanation: Sensitive Data Protection inspects text and structured data for PII, supports de-identification (redaction, masking, FPE), and integrates with BigQuery and Cloud Storage.

question: To run a Jupyter notebook environment with GPUs and direct access to BigQuery, which Vertex AI feature is recommended?
options: A. Vertex AI Workbench (Managed notebooks or Instances)
B. Compute Engine VM with manual installs
correct: A. Vertex AI Workbench (Managed notebooks or Instances)
explanation: Vertex AI Workbench provides managed JupyterLab notebooks with GPU support, BigQuery/Cloud Storage integrations, and lifecycle scripts.

question: What is a good rule of thumb when an imbalanced classification task shows extremely high accuracy but poor recall on the minority class?
options: A. Use class-weighting, resampling (SMOTE, undersampling), or alternative loss functions; evaluate with precision/recall/F1 or PR-AUC, not raw accuracy
B. Train longer with no other changes
C. Switch metrics to plain accuracy
correct: A. Use class-weighting, resampling (SMOTE, undersampling), or alternative loss functions; evaluate with precision/recall/F1 or PR-AUC, not raw accuracy
explanation: Imbalanced data inflates accuracy. Class weighting/resampling and minority-aware loss functions improve recall; precision/recall, F1, and PR-AUC are appropriate metrics.
